newsitem.title: UK: MOBIL ISSUES FORCE MAJEURE ON OSO REPAIR DELAY.
newsitem.headline: MOBIL ISSUES FORCE MAJEURE ON OSO REPAIR DELAY.

text.p: Mobil Corp said on Friday it had issued letters of force majeure to lifters of Nigerian Oso informing them of delays to loadings because of a longer than expected shutdown.

A Mobile spokesman added by telephone the company hoped to restart production on Saturday morning. A technical failure prompted a shutdown of the 100,000 barrels per day condensate field early last week.
The spokesman said he understood the letters of force majeure had been issued on Thursday. He added four cargoes would be delayed by about two weeks but there were no cancellations.
The spokesman said the force majeure had been issued to what he called affected customers but gave no details.
Oil traders had said on Tuesday that as a result of the shutdown loading dates for August cargoes had been put back by about 10 days.

The field, which the U.S. major operates with the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) in a joint venture known as Mobil Nigeria Producing Unlimited, was shut down after an incident at one platform.
Mobil said earlier in the week it hoped production would be back to its normal level "in a few days".
"We will not cut corners on safety just to get production running," the spokesman said. He added the field had been unable to obtain deliveries of repair materials as quickly as had been planned.
An investigation had been launched into the delays in resuming production at the field, he said.

Nigeria's production of condensate, an extra-light hydrocarbon which is not counted as part of the country's 1.865 million bpd OPEC quota, is expected to reach 200,000 bpd when stage two of the NNPC/Mobil project comes on stream early next year.
